content.user_title: Control AI Coding Plans Before Execution
content.value_statement: Complex AI coding changes can move too quickly and create avoidable risk. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured approval workflow before execution begins.
actual_capabilities: Defines when approval is required for database, API, dependency, deployment, and architecture changes.
Provides minimal and comprehensive plan templates with risks, alternatives, testing, rollback, and time estimates.
Describes explicit approval, modification, rejection, and revised-plan workflows.
Shows how to store proposed, approved, rejected, and completed plans for later reference.
Guides agents to detect plan deviations and request renewed approval before continuing.
Includes example slash commands for creating, reviewing, approving, rejecting, and tracking plans.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not implement a command runner or storage backend.
It relies on the agent and user to follow the approval workflow consistently.
It does not validate plans against a real repository or production environment.
It does not enforce permissions outside the active AI assistant session.

use_cases.title: Approve Risky Refactors
use_cases.description: Review proposed architecture, file changes, risks, and rollback steps before an AI assistant changes many files.

use_cases.title: Control Database Changes
use_cases.description: Require a clear migration plan before schema, RLS, index, or data changes are made.

use_cases.title: Document Agent Decisions
use_cases.description: Keep records of approved, rejected, and completed plans so future sessions can use prior preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple approval checkpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short plan for this change before implementation. Include files affected, risks, estimated time, and ask for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Require Approval for Risky Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before database, dependency, deployment, or breaking API changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before making this risky change, prepare a detailed approval plan. Include alternatives, rollback steps, tests, and the exact approval options.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a Rejected Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the first plan needs user changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the previous plan based on my feedback. Show what changed, what risks remain, and ask for approval again before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Track a Plan Deviation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow when implementation no longer matches the approved plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current implementation path with the approved plan. Identify any deviation, explain the impact, and ask whether to proceed, revise, or revert.

output_examples.input: Add Stripe subscription billing to the app.
output: A structured plan lists new Stripe client, checkout, webhook, pricing, package, environment example, and database migration changes.
The plan explains why Stripe Checkout was chosen, notes webhook and state sync risks, estimates time, and asks for approve, modify, or reject.

output_examples.input: Continue the approved implementation, but use a different payment flow.
output: A deviation notice compares the approved approach with the new approach.
The assistant explains affected files, risk changes, and asks for renewed approval before continuing.

output_examples.input: Show the status of the approved plan.
output: A progress summary shows approved time, current step, completed tasks, remaining tasks, and the next planned action.
The summary keeps implementation status tied to the approved plan.

best_practices: Require explicit approval before complex, risky, breaking, or production-impacting changes.
Include risks, alternatives, testing strategy, and rollback steps in detailed plans.
Ask for renewed approval when implementation meaningfully diverges from the approved plan.
anti_patterns: Treating silence or unclear feedback as approval to proceed.
Creating vague plans that omit files, risks, tests, or rollback details.
Continuing after a major deviation without showing the user the impact.

faq.question: Does this skill execute approval commands?
faq.answer: No. It describes a workflow and example commands, but it does not provide executable tooling.

faq.question: When should approval be required?
faq.answer: Use approval for database changes, breaking APIs, dependency updates, file deletions, deployments, and broad refactors.

faq.question: Can this work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written as agent guidance and can be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: What should a good plan include?
faq.answer: A good plan names affected files, rationale, alternatives, risks, tests, rollback steps, and estimated time.

faq.question: What happens if the user rejects a plan?
faq.answer: The skill recommends saving the rejection, learning from the reason, and not proceeding with implementation.

faq.question: Does it protect production systems automatically?
faq.answer: No. It improves decision discipline, but it does not enforce repository permissions or production access controls.
